article_title: A novel Z-number based multi-stage assessment framework for problem-based learning in practical courses.
citation: Yu Limin, Chen Zhe, Qin Zeyu. (2026). A novel Z-number based multi-stage assessment framework for problem-based learning in practical courses. PLOS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0349114
title: Z-MABAC multi-stage assessment framework for PBL practical courses
description: The article introduces a data-driven assessment framework that integrates Z-number theory with the MABAC method to rank students in PBL practical courses. Z-numbers pair each evaluation with a reliability measure, so that 'assessments with higher uncertainty exert proportionally less influence on the final decision.' The framework runs in three phases — Pass check, Score determination, and Grading — aligned with PBL pedagogy, and uses a hybrid Entropy-CRITIC weighting scheme to set criteria weights objectively.
requirements: Multiple stakeholder evaluator groups (peers, instructors, industry experts) providing Z-number linguistic assessments
Conversion of Z-number evaluations into triangular fuzzy numbers before ranking
constraints: Validated only within a single PBL practical course context; the authors note broader generalizability requires further validation across cohorts, courses, and institutions
target_learners: undergraduate students in application-focused practical courses
target_learning_goals: holistic performance assessment including teamwork, problem-solving, and project deliverable quality
examples: Applied in the course 'Design investigation and analysis' with 24 students in four peer groups of six
